eyebrow: Three dimensions a generic model misses

steps.label: Data sensitivity
steps.sub: Training data, retrieved context, and what could be memorized

steps.label: Autonomy level
steps.sub: Read-only chatbot vs. an agent that can call tools and act

steps.label: User trust boundary
steps.sub: Vetted internal users vs. anyone on the public internet

code:
Spoofing              -> impersonating a user to the model
Tampering             -> prompt injection / data poisoning
Repudiation           -> no logging of prompts & decisions
Info disclosure        -> system-prompt & training-data leakage
Denial of service      -> resource-exhaustion prompts
Elevation of privilege -> tool-calling abused beyond scope
caption: Microsoft's established framework, read against an AI system's real components.

eyebrow: Worked example: a refund-ticket RAG chatbot
code:
System: support chatbot, retrieves KB, can call
        "create refund ticket" API

Data sensitivity  -> KB may contain customer PII
Autonomy          -> NOT read-only: can create a real ticket
Trust boundary    -> any logged-in customer, unvetted

=> Tampering + Elevation of Privilege = top priority
   for the Lesson 25 red-team scope
